Hello everyone, friends. I hope someone else remembers me after almost a month since I showed you the project I'm working on. We are talking about Lessons In Love Remake. Today I'm here to share with you some updates on where I'm at right now and what I've done since the beginning of this project. I hope you are still interested in this. So, at the moment I have finished the concept phase of the whole game and would like to share with you what I have been able to do in these few months. I left a link to the screenshots, they are in this order to make it look like you are clicking on the buttons or scrolling.

P.S.1. I want to remind you not to pay attention to the inconsistency of names, titles, groups, images and all that, because for now this is just a concept and I tried to do it as soon as possible.
P.S.2. I also want to note that these screenshots do not take into account all the wishes and comments of the community that were given to me a month ago. But they will be taken into account in the future, of course. It's just that at the moment it's rather expensive to redo the layout. So I left it to the coding stage.
P.S.3. I also have a version of all these screenshots with indicators on the icons (red dots), but I will not post them here, because they are the same thing, just know that such notifications will be where there is any unviewed content, and yes , they can also be customized.
P.S.4. Please don't be intimidated by the overly glassy interface. In the working version, all this will be customizable to the point that all these effects can be turned off. For now, I've just done what I like)


The game itself


In-game phone


That's all I've done for now. I hope you enjoy what I have done and I will be very happy if you leave any feedback. Your wishes, criticism, ideas for improvement are very valuable to me, I will definitely take all this into account. In the meantime, the concept stage is over. Next up is the development phase. Now I will gradually write the interface code and all that. I will try to put together a working alpha build as soon as possible so that the community can push the buttons and see how everything works.

Those that occur organically within the story are not animated.
Repeatable sex scenes that you unlock through gameplay are animated.

posts.content_html_raw:
Selebus is fine, just weird and a bit obnoxious, he's neither as good as those who like him make it out to be nor as bad as those who dislike him believe.
His tenacity and work ethic is outright scary, character expressions and scenes are top notch and his writing is so elusive that even after 3 years I can't really tell whether it's godly and he had almost everything figured out from the get go or if he's been bullshiting us all this time and making shit up along the way.
Though I must say, he really needs more people to tell him how it is, neither demonizing nor worshipping him, the game could be so much better if he implements some QOL. Like, why the fuck do we need to remember random bits of information spread across several events for resets, or have to randomly navigate that horrible sandbox everytime a new update drops until we finds something in the particular order the game wants us to do?
Which is shame, the game is good but it could be so much better if it was more intuitive, we shouldn't need a mod to do literally anything in this game, or people hitting their head against the wall until something happens to drop a guide, really hoping that one "remake" guy makes it through, because although I love this game it's also very frustrating sometimes.

posts.content_html_raw:
A very literal calm before the storm or just pure subversion of expectations, teasing improvement on all the characters because 'nothing will go wrong ever again'

Ami's reaction to getting slapped and told off was more of a 'Wow, what a fun toy you became' sort of thing imo, her actions after the fact were tame but that felt very on par with the idea that this beach chain was just a tease and reprieve from whatever soul crushing comes next given most of it felt like it was setting up Ayane to get killed off in the woods.

The Sekai flashback actually made me sad instead of creeped out because it felt like it wasn't actually an abusive situation for a second so I probably need therapy and god damn Ami(?) is scary.

Nodoka did Nodoka things and the theory of being an actual daughter is terrifying. Her eyes are close enough to Ami/Sekai's and the notion that she knows things about Sekai and Akira as poets enough to blow off Futaba and hover around Ami is also concerning. Akira's disposition to willingly offer her to Haruka yet shrink at the idea of others because Nodoka is a conduit for his pain? Probably the most fucked up event and relationship.

This was paralleled by the Niki (best girl) scenes in a way? (Very big mad no Imani/Wakana/Niki 4some, though opened up a Futaba Imani 3some?) The different understandings and acceptance of Akira's functioning, Niki understanding Akira out of 'love' and/or desperation to Nodokas acceptance of Akira's worst parts out of what seems to be curiosity?

Dorm 2 girls were hard to not pick as winners for this event in the minor chances we got. Chika felt resigned to the loss from the get go and Otoha admitted the worst possible thing she could have while going 'I know you're at least kinda cool so you won't blab' (And i really don't like Otoha because Rin is up there on best girls) while Sana just...said she was horny for Sensei and ran away? ('Yasu' also said her brother wants to watch her do the nasty and that's all sorts of on par for this game fucked)

The rest of the event was basically just wholesome with very little even focusing on Akira and more the relationships between the girls. I don't like Kirin but I'm glad she's slowly being accepted by others, I'm glad Io suddenly spent the day with 1 person she can tolerate that isn't Uta, and then one more, and then Kirin. I'm glad Touka is feeling comfortable enough to raise her voice and break her rich girl persona and 'start' a conflict because she wants to protect Yasu and dig her nails into sensei.

This has been the first patch I've had to wait for (and oh god waiting another month is actually hell? how have any of you lasted this long?) but I'm happy enough with how everything turned out because it was a nice 'break' from everything going to shit...Even if it's just a setup for MORE things to go bad.

posts.content_html_raw:
Some rambling thoughts and observations after finishing the update and a half night of sleep:
- Let's see how next events unfold, but I'm satisfied with how the update ended. We were probably too focused on psycho Ami as the source of bad things to happen and sort of acting like Ayane as spectators. Now we have to be more aware of where the big punchs are going to come from. I like that, its a good kind of uncertainty.

- The "Maya is evil" crowd surely is happy and feeling validated after the update. Looking forward to read their thoughts.

- All the wholesomness and fanservice felt so weird, for a number of reasons. I mean, it was welcome, we don't get much of that in this game but it actually made me uneasy. Also a bit weird having it combined with was happening at the time. The subtext was like "Hey girls, it's so cool that we start to get along better and try to put ourselves in other people's shoes. We are becoming such good friends!" "Yeah I agree, and since we are at it, we should maaaybe care a little more about the girls that have been in the jungle for 20 hours with no water and food and probably already bitten by a poisonous snake" "Naahh, they are fiiiiiine".

- So do you think the daisy hairpin it's just a gift or an actual source of power? And that's what giving Ayane her new found confidence, and why she seems to retain the memory of Himawari.

- Hey Otoha, remember when you wondered why Nodoka and you become friends. Well, after hearing your confession to Akira I think I have an idea. That being said, I like her character more now. I mean, it's not that I like her but now I'm provided with better reasons to hate her instead of her just being boring.

- Chika and Rin belong to each other and there's nothing more to be said.

- Hey Sel, I'm tired of you priving us from the good stuff. Sex scenes happening off screen is one thing, but why didn't you let me appreciate Yumi's poetry in its entirety? This is the second time Yumi's art is censored. The first being the work she did on Nodoka's face which we didn't get to see. Fuck you.

posts.content_html_raw:
Regarding the whole Ami/Psycho Ami/Maya dynamic.

Maya is an unreliable source -- I'm not saying she's lying, but that she's already shown to have not interpreted the data she had properly, which has led to a number of wrong conclusions so far.

She may have seen Psycho Ami, but that doesn't mean she saw Ami go psycho. It could have been one of the angels piloting Ami, a shapeshifter posing as Ami (presumably, the existence of Himawarii implies that there might be others), or one of the other versions of Ami floating around (Bound Nao, broken Ami, etc). Not armed with the knowledge that the other potential Ami's or angelic abilities exist, she put 2 and 2 together and didn't realize that she got 22, not 4.

posts.content_html_raw:
Selebus is like the school bully going "i'm gonna hit ya! I'm gonna hit ya!" and then never does it, at least in the case of this patch
I guess that could only foreshadow worse stuff later on, although i will say haruko's scene and the mom scene were both hard to stomach but at least not directly damaging to any of the characters so it ended on kind of a happy note

I don't think Maya is necessarily lying about Ami, just that this time around, Sensei is Sensei himself, and also, if we assume that other characters' interpersonal relationships are reset whenever Sensei is reset, then it's fair to assume Ayane and Maya both have at least somewhat a stronger bond with Ami now than they might've in the past when she went berserk. Things are clearly shown to be different than the past this time around, so even something as Ami going psycho doesn't necessarily have to happen (but still could have happened in the past).

Nodoka is clearly interested in Sekai (and either really really really good at guessing or might even have a direct connection to Sekai, judging from her "horror story"). She's now officially sus alongside Tsuneyo.

Things I didn't quite decipher: the line right after Ayane has been dropped off in the forest (basically saying, of the 4, one of the people there is not who they appear to be, and it's not the one you assume -- basically our first guess would be Ami, which means, there might be something going on with either Touka or Yasu from what i gleaned into it?)
Also the line about 3 moons and Yasu only being able to see 2. The colors of the moons in that scene made me assume they symbolize Ayane, Ami and Maya, rather than just the 3 gods, but I don't really get what it's about, either way. It could be just the 3rd god concealing her presence from Yasu, as the 1st and 2nd god seem to be kinda aligned together to some extent and the 3rd god now seems to be sort of aligned against them (loosely speaking of course).

Reasons because I wanna talk more about this game lmao.

S+

Niki: Actually a crime she's a side girl. Childhood friend Tsundere Ex GF Idol loyal to you because many faults understanding of every choice you make somehow? If Sekai wasn't apparently fucking supernatural/a massive predator Niki just wins the game before it starts. Hell you can just give me the Niki + Akira ending and I'm happy.

Wakana: I want to fucking die. Massive W content and character, might be sad to ruin her relationship but yknow... not sad enough to stop me. (I am a bad person).

Yumi: I clearly have a thing for Tsundere characters. Yumi feels alot more fleshed out as a character though that has gone through alot of changes and deserves the best... Or at least the money she keeps getting cheated out of. Genuinely a great person to who she cares about even if it doesn't seem like it - Chika and Chinami

Tsuneyo: Get leeked bro, she's the most attractive woman on the beach. Assertive, funny, 'aware', ride or die character. I don't want her to have lewd scenes because she's perfect the way she is, but also lewd scenes when so we can properly welcome noodles as our son?

Rin: Bruh it's Rin. You don't be a good homie because Chika is mid, you be a good homie because Rin is Rin. Confused Bisexual Disaster that you literally just want the best for? She's just a best friend you have conflicting feelings over no matter what route.

Futaba: Dorm 4 is fucking op. Futaba is still a work in progress but she feels the most 'real' among the cast, Nodoka understands. Honestly feels like one of the best fits for Sensei and I would take the 'Futaba only' route (if Niki didn't exist and this game wasn't designed to hurt us)

S:

Maya: Again... Tsundere things. Shrine maiden outfit. Lore is seeming that she is danger but assuming she's really gone through so many resets who knows how old she is mentally at this point. I think the whole idea is that all she wants is to get through the reset hell and finally be with Akira without any loops, She might want everyone else to eat shit and die first but I respect the effort. Further updates will either propel her to the top or the bottom...

Touka: Mommy.

Kaori: Friendburger is good No smut allowed, Sekai stay away.

Yasu/Sana: Protecc. Fuck you gods.

Sara: Take that you dirty Milf. Also she just like us frfr. She has a lot of scenes and a lot of lore that isn't explored, despite her shitty bar name she is one of the characters I wanna see so much more of and is actively confused by.

A:

Makoto: Wild character arc, she wants you to put her at S+ but sadly I don't think it'll ever happen. Alot of development but she's still just... 'The depressed suicidal character' Witch outfit is 10/10 tho.

Nodoka: Enigma. Can see Sekai? Himawari? Agree on Wakana chasing. Loses massive points for Matador. Gained points back later. Volatile ranking but she enables alot of dialogue and thought everytime she shows up when it's not related to lesbianism. Also enables alot of lesbianism.

Tsubasa: Didn't rat us out. Mommy x2. House!. SCARY AF.

Yuki: Feels like close to Rin level Homie but not developed enough, supports higher rankings well however.

Maki: Lewd queen trying her best to fill a newly created hole...heh filling a hole.

B:

Imani: Potential to either rise or fall greatly in later rankings but is currently just a comedic echo riding the flow of everyone around her.

Miku: Again potential to rise or fall. Tomboy is ++. Airhead is -. She's supportive of anyone and everyone as long as she can still get what she now wants... Wildcard tbh.

Noriko: Should probably be much higher but competing with her sister is a massive oof. Everything she does feels outclassed by someone else in the cast yet that's probably the point. She is excellent at making you feel uncomfortable while trying to make you love her.

C:

Pretty much all of these are 'Oh no i'm so in love with Sensei i've forgotten how to be myself' in an aspect or another. Sure they have arcs and reasons but they need more before i can rate them higher.

Chika: Takes the lead because of the Chinami and Tsubasa plot but she's so committed to believing Sensei is committed she can't see any of the obvious shit happening

Ayane: Was/Is gaining a lot of traction and growth but honestly outside of her confronting Kirin and now Ami she's back to the 'I cling to sensei and say i love him every scene' trope

Ami: Same as Ayane tbh. Horny Incest trope does nothing for me and the more that gets revealed the scarier she is, it could work in her favor if done well but we'll have to see how she gets fleshed out.

Haruka: In denial, slowly accepting that she's actually just as bad as Sensei is, emphasized greatly in recent events. She was just a shitty person before but now she's a REALLY shitty person. It's interesting in a bad way but she stands out more because of it.

D:

Molly: I hate that i understand most of her geek speak. It's hard to like Molly because she goes against all the presets and is quite frankly written to be hard to like. She hasn't gotten much screentime outside of bad situations and weebnotes so tbh she can probably only go up or just stay average. Have her dye her hair and cosplay real hard or something idk.

Io: Respectful character lacking respect for others. Trauma on a degree we don't know yet. She's cute and best friend material but needs more time.

Uta: Dual personality gimmick between Uta-Chan and real Uta has worn off. Understandably fearful of getting close to Sensei but is also hiding feelings from Io? again ranking low because of less character development but is more or less a package deal with Io atm.

Osako: Not much development. Wakana Sub. I wanna be her tho on god? Raising affection is a pain in the ass and literally just going through her to get to Wakana. I am a bad person.

Otoha: Fuck Otoha, She's only above Rika and the wizards because of her beach scene. Bad homie until proven otherwise.

F:

Rika: Not fleshed out enough but disaster lesbians are fun.

Karin: Too conservative that the gimmick has worn off. Needs more development because she's on the verge of just being annoying.

Kirin: See Karin but replace conservative with horny. Is developing as a character by admitting her feelings but she's already built the unlikable reputation.

Wizards: Are Wizards. I can't compete with their spell knowledge and business prowess so this makes me dislike them greatly -- It's fine if they show up in scenes when appropriate but I have no desire for anything lewd and also Nao is sus af.

Reasons because I wanna talk more about this game lmao.

S+

Niki: Actually a crime she's a side girl. Childhood friend Tsundere Ex GF Idol loyal to you because many faults understanding of every choice you make somehow? If Sekai wasn't apparently fucking supernatural/a massive predator Niki just wins the game before it starts. Hell you can just give me the Niki + Akira ending and I'm happy.

Wakana: I want to fucking die. Massive W content and character, might be sad to ruin her relationship but yknow... not sad enough to stop me. (I am a bad person).

Yumi: I clearly have a thing for Tsundere characters. Yumi feels alot more fleshed out as a character though that has gone through alot of changes and deserves the best... Or at least the money she keeps getting cheated out of. Genuinely a great person to who she cares about even if it doesn't seem like it - Chika and Chinami

Tsuneyo: Get leeked bro, she's the most attractive woman on the beach. Assertive, funny, 'aware', ride or die character. I don't want her to have lewd scenes because she's perfect the way she is, but also lewd scenes when so we can properly welcome noodles as our son?

Rin: Bruh it's Rin. You don't be a good homie because Chika is mid, you be a good homie because Rin is Rin. Confused Bisexual Disaster that you literally just want the best for? She's just a best friend you have conflicting feelings over no matter what route.

Futaba: Dorm 4 is fucking op. Futaba is still a work in progress but she feels the most 'real' among the cast, Nodoka understands. Honestly feels like one of the best fits for Sensei and I would take the 'Futaba only' route (if Niki didn't exist and this game wasn't designed to hurt us)

S:

Maya: Again... Tsundere things. Shrine maiden outfit. Lore is seeming that she is danger but assuming she's really gone through so many resets who knows how old she is mentally at this point. I think the whole idea is that all she wants is to get through the reset hell and finally be with Akira without any loops, She might want everyone else to eat shit and die first but I respect the effort. Further updates will either propel her to the top or the bottom...

Touka: Mommy.

Kaori: Friendburger is good No smut allowed, Sekai stay away.

Yasu/Sana: Protecc. Fuck you gods.

Sara: Take that you dirty Milf. Also she just like us frfr. She has a lot of scenes and a lot of lore that isn't explored, despite her shitty bar name she is one of the characters I wanna see so much more of and is actively confused by.

A:

Makoto: Wild character arc, she wants you to put her at S+ but sadly I don't think it'll ever happen. Alot of development but she's still just... 'The depressed suicidal character' Witch outfit is 10/10 tho.

Nodoka: Enigma. Can see Sekai? Himawari? Agree on Wakana chasing. Loses massive points for Matador. Gained points back later. Volatile ranking but she enables alot of dialogue and thought everytime she shows up when it's not related to lesbianism. Also enables alot of lesbianism.

Tsubasa: Didn't rat us out. Mommy x2. House!. SCARY AF.

Yuki: Feels like close to Rin level Homie but not developed enough, supports higher rankings well however.

Maki: Lewd queen trying her best to fill a newly created hole...heh filling a hole.

B:

Imani: Potential to either rise or fall greatly in later rankings but is currently just a comedic echo riding the flow of everyone around her.

Miku: Again potential to rise or fall. Tomboy is ++. Airhead is -. She's supportive of anyone and everyone as long as she can still get what she now wants... Wildcard tbh.

Noriko: Should probably be much higher but competing with her sister is a massive oof. Everything she does feels outclassed by someone else in the cast yet that's probably the point. She is excellent at making you feel uncomfortable while trying to make you love her.

C:

Pretty much all of these are 'Oh no i'm so in love with Sensei i've forgotten how to be myself' in an aspect or another. Sure they have arcs and reasons but they need more before i can rate them higher.

Chika: Takes the lead because of the Chinami and Tsubasa plot but she's so committed to believing Sensei is committed she can't see any of the obvious shit happening

Ayane: Was/Is gaining a lot of traction and growth but honestly outside of her confronting Kirin and now Ami she's back to the 'I cling to sensei and say i love him every scene' trope

Ami: Same as Ayane tbh. Horny Incest trope does nothing for me and the more that gets revealed the scarier she is, it could work in her favor if done well but we'll have to see how she gets fleshed out.

Haruka: In denial, slowly accepting that she's actually just as bad as Sensei is, emphasized greatly in recent events. She was just a shitty person before but now she's a REALLY shitty person. It's interesting in a bad way but she stands out more because of it.

D:

Molly: I hate that i understand most of her geek speak. It's hard to like Molly because she goes against all the presets and is quite frankly written to be hard to like. She hasn't gotten much screentime outside of bad situations and weebnotes so tbh she can probably only go up or just stay average. Have her dye her hair and cosplay real hard or something idk.

Io: Respectful character lacking respect for others. Trauma on a degree we don't know yet. She's cute and best friend material but needs more time.

Uta: Dual personality gimmick between Uta-Chan and real Uta has worn off. Understandably fearful of getting close to Sensei but is also hiding feelings from Io? again ranking low because of less character development but is more or less a package deal with Io atm.

Osako: Not much development. Wakana Sub. I wanna be her tho on god? Raising affection is a pain in the ass and literally just going through her to get to Wakana. I am a bad person.

Otoha: Fuck Otoha, She's only above Rika and the wizards because of her beach scene. Bad homie until proven otherwise.

F:

Rika: Not fleshed out enough but disaster lesbians are fun.

Karin: Too conservative that the gimmick has worn off. Needs more development because she's on the verge of just being annoying.

Kirin: See Karin but replace conservative with horny. Is developing as a character by admitting her feelings but she's already built the unlikable reputation.

Wizards: Are Wizards. I can't compete with their spell knowledge and business prowess so this makes me dislike them greatly -- It's fine if they show up in scenes when appropriate but I have no desire for anything lewd and also Nao is sus af.

The sandbox itself is not bad, just the way it works when it comes to story progression, it was fun during the early game because we had lots of open ends and the game could be approached in multiple ways but as the game advances the quantity of events available are reduced and they are often tied to each other so you get to the end of this plotline before moving to the next which is fine, continuity and all, but then you have to farm 25 points with Osako which you can only see during the weekends or you should catch up with Yumi's events before going to the bathhouse with Chika for a better outcome.
Sel has recently been trying to chain events more often to reduce the maze, but it arguably got worse since now you gotta worry about 2 separate characters for a single chain that can be activated in unexpected ways such as the examples I used earlier (Chika-Tsubasa, Yuki-Sara).
All in all, I enjoy the sandbox elements, I like seeing new locations dropping with new characters, dialogue changing as you get close to them and more options getting unlocked, even more so since lots of places changed with chapter 3, I love the dialogue between Maya and Sensei when you call her at night for example.
To reduce some of the problems with the sandbox it would be good if the characters invited us sometimes instead of Sensei having to reach out to them every single time, have Molly call to hang out during Friday, or maybe Yuki asking for help at work, it would make it more natural and fluid, instead of requiring the player to try every single possible option until you find that one specific trigger you need.

AgumenticR said:
On another note, what do people think about Noriko and Maya apparently having a childhood pact that divides the city between them, and one that Maya feels so strongly about she is not visiting the Old half to this day?
Click to expand...
I was thoroughly confused during that TBH.

First is this pact was probably made before Sensei disappearing the second time, and it was not something in the pact that led to Sensei disappearing with Maya. Otherwise, it would greatly contradict what Noriko said in Loxosceles Reclusa, the "came out of nowhere" and "I took it upon myself to go out and find you". Plus, Noriko would never agree to any pact IF she knew the outcome of the pact would be like that, but this wasn't something she pointed out during the most recent beach conversation.

Second is that it's been circulating that a part of the reasons Maya not visiting old towns is because it's something existential; like something unexplainable will happen to her if she did go there. But, this would be disapproved if she is just sticking with the pact, a pact made with Noriko who seemingly doesn't have enough "world-shattering" attributes (in comparison to the likes of Ami or Nodoka). So this pact may not carry any god-related weight.

I.e., it's like two goddesses fighting for the same thing while not leaving their own realm due to supernatural reasons. But looking back on the past events, Noriko isn't really this type of character. She is at best a red herring created by Maya's prejudice because so far, Noriko really is a just nice person who can't help falling in love with a dickhead (well unless a weird plot twist comes out of nowhere and shows that she really is THE bad person)

Still, it's apparent that Maya now follows the pact due to different reasons now (the hard reset and everything), but as long as Noriko isn't on the same world-related boat with Maya, bringing up the pact to Noriko really doesn't mean a lot.

So to me, the pact might be more or less just a love rival thing (from Noriko, a stupid promise); it might be something only as serious as the Nakayama Sister Laws. I really want to think that this pact actually means something more to Sensei's past because of this scene, but I don't know how to make sense of it (even this post looks incoherent TBH, someone else help me out pls)

crustlord12 said:
I might have missed this, but is there an in-game lore reason that everyone is associating certain gods with certain seasons? I'm a bit lost on why everyone is calling HOPE winter, etc
Click to expand...
HOPE/Callous god is actually likely strongest in Summer. The Wire god/Calm god is likely strongest in Winter. Pareidolia/Concerned god is likely strongest in Spring.

Yasu has noted/Implied that her god slumbers in Winter and dislikes the cold:
more than once:
We also have "The Lust Eater" Book in 'A Life Of Prizes' that you get if you have chosen Callous, being hot:
and besides the Book mentioning eyes which is a Yasu god/HOPE thing, it also says something that heavily implies it is HOPE:

The god of wires being Winter is more of an educated guess thing as far as I can recall. Tsuneyo has implied to have a preference for Winter, so with that, and how she seems heavily related to this god, on top of Yasu/HOPE seemingly disliking Wires and Winter, it fits. We also have the 'A Life of Prizes' book that you get if you chose Calm, being called the "The Wire God" and it's notably cold:
and it responds like a computer:
So, it's not entirely clear but very likely that The Wire god is a Winter god.

There is also how Pareidolia implied the /// computer talk stuff is out of season in Summer in 'Ad Infinitum':
Which implies the /// computer talk is a Winter thing, and the Wire god is the one who tends to only speak that way. In a roundabout way implying the Wire god's season is Winter.

Now, as for Pareidolia, it has actually just implied that it is it's turn in Springtime:

As to why Seasons matter: Pareidolia has implied that Seasons affect the gods performance before it got one:
That on top of Yasu's god slumbering in Winter, etc, it's more or less confirmed that Seasons are important when it comes to the gods.

Also, just so you know what I'm talking about with the 'A Life of Prizes' Books, these are their names:
You're only supposed to have one Book 9, but I kinda cheated to save space. Anyway, If you chose Callous you get "The Lust Eater", if you chose Calm you get "The Wire God", and if you chose Concerned you get "The Dark".

Getting to learn how much was hiding beneath the surface of all these characters is really neat, Selly is quite good at character writing (but not game design, alas). Even Akira himself, who I thought was completely irredeemable in chapter 1, is slowly, ever so slowly, becoming less of a trash bin. I'm also a sucker for time loop/peggy sue stories, so the resets really hit the dopamine button.

My list, based more on who I find interesting than who I want to bone.


Rin/Niki: What's not to love? They're good at asserting their boundaries and give Akira plenty of sass. True homies.

Yasu: I really enjoy the "supernatural" parts of LiL, so it's natural her connection with HOPE gets a high rank. The fact that she's kind hearted when not possessed put her at the top, despite the proselytizing.

Touka: Competent, attractive, and good at taking care of people. Top waifu. Came very far very quickly in understanding the poor commoners.

Io: A catalyst for positive change in Akira. Hopefully she learns how to be less self-defeating.

Sara: I wish she was a main. A genuine sweetheart who's career troubles are crushingly relatable. Her most recent events propelled her to S rank.

Nao: Adorable. Seriously though what is her deal?

Uta: Adorable and hot at the same time, pray for my wallet.

Yumi: An asshole, but proven to be a decent person in spite of this. One of 3 people for whom Akira willingly gives of himself. Somehow triggers Akira's episodes despite the two having minimal history. Down a rank due to stagnation in their dynamic recently.

Sana: Protecc the smol. Rank up due to progress in coming out of her shell.

Maya: Controlling and deeply embittered, she's running out of revelations to offer and excuses to hide them. Down multiple ranks from where she began, because her "I know better" attitude is no longer justified.

Chika: Also down several ranks from where she began, due to stagnation. Friendly, outgoing, loving, and dependable, only Touka can match her as a waifu. Akira is exploiting her need for stability and affection, and I think subconsious jealousy is bringing out a snippy side of her. Willful obliviousness on her part to Akira's true nature has prevented her from doing anything interesting for some time.

Ayane: Started at the bottom, now she's here. Her gradual ascension from one-note Sensei groupie to multifaceted loop survivor is very welcome. Might be a bit too strong: I was hoping for Ami to be genuinely dangerous, but Ayane kneecapped that for now.

Otoha: Is in the process of badly mishandling her relationships, and I'm interested in seeing how far it falls. F in chat for Rin.

Makoto: I heavily relate to her depression and struggle with being unappreciated. Unlike most characters, who reveal parts of themselves that were hidden, Makoto has actually changed quite a bit over the course of LiL.

Kaori: Homieburger! Difficult to understand, somehow vulnerable to Sekai's influence. Surprisingly responsible and self-aware.

Tsuenyo: One of the few holdouts against Akira's inexplicable magnetism, but it's waning. I didn't think I would like her, until she used her stoicism to clown Akira three times in the same event. She's been putting him in his place ever since.

Molly: Started as an immersion breaking one-note trash bin. Her struggle to overcome culture clashes, unrequited feelings, and the events of Halloween have humanized her.

Noriko: Was hiding a sincere heart of gold underneath the illusion of a yandere.

Rika: Low screentime thus far, but I like her for the same reasons I like Rin.

Futaba: I want to like her, but Nodoka's constant presence next to her drags her down. Her new companionship with Imai is neat, but she doesn't move the plot forward at all.

Karin: I'm a fan of her archetype, but nothing new has happened with her in... forever. Desperately in need of progression.

Miku: The brainless airhead schtick really doesn't do it for me.

Haruka: I empathized a lot with her loneliness and sexual frustration, but unfortunately she's just kind of terrible all around, and not interesting enough to make up for it.

Tsubasa: Has the potential to be rated a lot higher, but a lack of screen time is killing it.

Tsukasa: Irritating twat of a kid. At her best when she and Akira are getting on each other's nerves.

Imani: Why is she here? The only thing she's done so far is give Futaba someone to bond with over body issues.

Wakana/Maki/Yuki: Same problem as Miku.

Chinami: I'm truly not sure why she gets on my nerves, but she does. Oh well.

Ami: Has stood resolutely between Akira and anything interesting since day one, and she'll stay in the bin until Psycho Ami actually starts getting shit done.

Nodoka: Currently just a worse version of Akira. Perhaps she'll escape when her mad visions become more prevalent, or if she uncovers interesting things about Ami or Sekai.

Osako: Ended up as Wakana's satellite. Has yet to do anything of relevance.

Kirin: As toxic as people come, and actively brings down many scenes she's in with her excessive focus on sex. There's hints of a character growth arc, but until something comes of it, trash will remain in the trash bin.

It's somewhat still up in the air.

The main things that I've noticed that is likely important when it comes to the accident besides it being when Ami was 7, and it killed her parents is:
  • In 'The mysterious abundance of chickens': Sensei seemingly removed "strips of steel from her body" and "saw it all":
    "Her" is likely Sekai.
  • In 'First contact': Sensei seems to imply he was in a moving car, a moving car crashed into a wall, and it was "Us driving":
    Also seemingly there was a moon out, and Sensei also asks "Why did it have to be him?":
  • In 'The way it scatters' If you're fucking Ami: Ami reveals she watched her parents die:
  • In the Japanese 'Peekaboo' event where Sekai is restored: Sekai's car seems to show up and be Yellow:
    And in 'Baby Finches': It's the Yellow car that seems to crash:
Now, overall, it hasn't really been confirmed what happened.

Still, I am beginning to think Sensei was driving Sekai's car with Sekai and Ami in it, but he crashed into another car that just so happened to be Nozomu's, and they both wrecked. Sekai and Nozomu ended up dead (Nozomu burned to death becoming a ball of light, while Sekai became mangled into looking like a tree with roots of wire), while Ami and Sensei ended up "broken". I can also see Sensei considering his brother as a "Wall", due to him being the thing between Sensei and Sekai (The World).

Of course, I could be way off.

and catalogs it:

and how it's the last of it's kind, implying that whatever it is, is Notable. I also get the sense it likes to watch things happen like Nao:

Overall: I'm thinking Nao is on a higher level than the Seasonal gods. They might be so beneath it, their resources are it's trash. Not entirely sure about the "4th god" though.

I thought this was obvious, Sel is the king of anticlimatic endings.
Remember insane Makoto in chap 1? It got me so hooked, but then she suddenly became normal in chap 2. She doesn't even question what happened in bluejay now that she's aware (yet).
Remember when Rin felt empty after dating Otoha? She also became normal in chap 3, or to be more accurate she got sidetracked by her conflicts with Otoha. And while I do think that fits with her character, I feel like there could've been a better resolution for that story.
There's also Sara's bar and Yumi's job, which I've talked about in a previous post about how they are just there to explore the characters. There's a lot more examples I can talk about too.
It feels like the stories that do get strong moments are planned from the start. Maya and Niki are the two biggest examples.
Anyways, Sel's biggest strength is getting people attached to the cast, and I will still be here for the cute girl banter. I've talked about this a lot already. But if the story continues to go at the pace of 0.33 and we don't get some really big revelation by the end of chap 3, Sel's gonna lose a decent chunk of his following.

It's not an ending, the psycho Ami arc was just put into question. Something that was needed for a couple of reasons:
First off, the Ayane character. She was already getting on my nerves this update. Of course I get why she acted like that, made total sense. The story needs to move on and she was not allowing that.

The other reason is that we were putting almost all our focus on psycho Ami while now we have more food for thought. Look, I understand people feeling gaslighted (again), but now we have two characters (Maya, Himawari) saying opposite things. Depending on how events unfold, one of them will have more cred and we'll have something to hold on to.

I think this is all purpousely leading to make us question Maya more and more. At first, she was our beacon light, almost taking her word as gospel no matter how many times she would say that she knows little to nothing. We simply didn't have anything else.

It turns out that we were building castles in the sand, and now Maya will suffer the backlash. She will be accused of being a villain by both us and the characters, while most likely she is just a victim of perception.

So, Random Theory Time: Noriko and Maya's deal, may have broke an already broken Sensei:
So, after the last update, we know Noriko and Maya made a pact as kids which involved Sensei:
Noriko seemed to have to stay in the Old District and Maya had to stay in, I guess, everywhere else, and if Sensei was in the place they couldn't be, they had to let him go until he came back to their side. Until he chose to come back to them.

Now, what some may not remember is that Maya implied what actually caused Sensei to leave Noriko (with Maya):
And the major implication is:
Maya used Sex to control Sensei in his broken state at the time, or as Noriko puts it:
Maya took advantage of him, which also involved Maya:
Convincing Sensei he was all alone.

This is likely why Noriko claims Maya forced Sensei to choose:
And seems to be how Maya kept Noriko away:
She used the deal, sex, and Sensei's mental state to, well, make it seem like the Nakayama's didn't exist, and didn't need to.

Overall: It seems like we might know why Sensei "abandoned" the Nakayama's and "chose" Maya.

This also might be why he "breaks" when Maya gets too close, and why he has seemed to forget everything even prior to the resets, unlike everyone else, when there's a "New" Sensei. Maya may have broken his mind even more than it was, and now his mind freaks out when she gets too close as some sort of self defense mechanism. Of course, there's likely a lot more to it.
As for why Maya still avoids the Old District after all this time:
I think it's likely for the same reason she remains a shrine maiden:
She doesn't want to risk breaking the deal in case it influences her survivability.

Click to expand...
It's a poem from William Blake (1757–1827), called Infant Joy.

I have no name
I am but two days old.—
What shall I call thee?
I happy am
Joy is my name,—
Sweet joy befall thee!

Pretty joy!
Sweet joy but two days old,
Sweet joy I call thee;
Thou dost smile.
I sing the while
Sweet joy befall thee.

The common interpretation is that it celebrates the miracle of life (that or it's an infant being given a name and the mother celebrates).
Some website I checked on instead says that it's a discussion between the mother and the infant, with the mom asking what the infant should be called, and the infant says that his name will be Joy, since he is happy.

Now that the summer event is gone and we seem to be reaching the end of chapter, are there any girl that has made you completely reevaluate her character lately?

Most of this has actually been quite consistent throughout most of the game's lifespan. I'll just comment on some recent changes.

Kirin has been my #1 since the scene with Ayane at the beach and her scene after the Molly incident is one of the best in the game, but she's been dropping a bit now that she's starting to behave more like a normal person. Makoto has risen in my opinion quite steadily over the course of the game's life span. She has a pretty good arc, I think. And while Miku still isn't my favorite or anything, I would've probably put her in F tier at the start.

My mind don't really register the pet name Aki-kun well; Sekai used it as short for Akira, but separately Aki itself in kanji can be (an almost unambiguous one as well) written as 秋, which means Fall/Autumn, a season apparently Kumon-mi is about to have due to the rising of the third god.


What if the third god is some kind of separated, sealed off mentality of Akira after the accident that represents the Aki-kun back then? The third god has always been lacking descriptions in physical forms compared to the first two, and has been more portrayed as an incarnation of mental ideas: voice inside your head, embodiment of perception (Paredolia), etc. So the question becomes if it's at all possible that this voice, perception, personality, or whatever you want to call it, originates from a very OG version of Akira whose mind hasn't been traumatized, broken, and wiped clean to a point that the original can be viewed as a different individual compared to all the other Sensei iterations.

It surprised me that so many people are putting Ami at the top of the list when it comes to motherhood. She's already proven to be abusive, cruel, and manipulative to her friends, and that's not a good sign of how she's going to treat a child. She's probably the only one I'd believe would actually harm her kid. She seems like the type who would love the kid at first but eventually see the younger version of herself as competition, whether or not anything is happening between the kid and Sensei.

Of course, this is all going off the fact that I believe Ami's an absolute psycho. And my anger at all of you for not putting Imani where she belongs at the top of the list. So my opinion could be extremely biased.

Despite my dropping affinity for Ami after each update, I do think being abusive, cruel, and manipulative can miraculously co-exist with being a good mother at least in the fictional setting (if you factor in serving as a bad example to your children then it's a different story).

Ami's branded belief "Nothing matters but this person" is a type of servitude highly prioritized to the person she loves, a necessary feature for being a good mother. Her subject now is Sensei, but it's likely expandable from Sensei to her future incest baby. She is willing and capable of providing unrequited services while showing no apparent distaste to kids; so I think at least this part Ami should receive her credits. However, it's indeed still up for debate whether it is truly unrequited, as we know now Ami even has extended her manipulative methods on Sensei more than once to keep him around and dependent.

Being a bad friend is merely a side effect, or an expansion of that "Nothing matters but this person" attitude (of course as her friends or from player perspective that's not merely at all).

The only example I can think of which may be relatable is Cersei Lannister from GoT, someone who excels in all bad human traits but also will stop at nothing for her children (whether Cersei is a good mother or not is something worth debating, but hopefully I get my point across)

With all that being said, however, do I want Ami to be my mom? FUCK NO! I want Touka!

S:
Touka: The least corrupted so far. Might still want to murder Tsukasa but who doesn't? is the perfect mix of her mother and available resources.

A:
Futaba: Corrupted but still grounded. Probably capable of holding her own but still getting what she needs out of Sensei somehow (Insert mommy milkers joke), doesn't have parents immediately available to help her but is in contact with them + Rika/Rin/unnamed parent/nodoka(!)/Otoha would gladly help.

Maki: Maki is a fucking good mom ok? it's not her fault Makoto loves her dad more Maki is trying her god damn best the only way she knows how. Should honestly be S tier but knowledge warps perception... This hurts to write.

Imani: Imani is kinda just fucking grounded overall. She's smart and is overcoming her 'flaws'. Good sense of humor and overall just seems capable as a human. Probably isn't ready for children but this is using the assumption they turn into adults similar to fire emblem shenanigans*cough*

Rika: Rin is a good girl. She might have bad coping habits and depression but you really can't avoid that in children, the most you can do is support them. She might actually kinda suck because she relies on Rin alot more and Rin also seems to favor her other mom.. but at the same time Rin lets her stay in her dorm, doesn't raise hell when Rika starts working at the school and doesn't even argue much against the idea of Sensei and Rika getting together. Both her and her daughter might be disaster lesbians but they'll always have each other.

Tsuneyo: Noodles is a free roam shapeshifting bird god living their best life ready to murder Sensei (I can relate). Tsuneyo is an OP single mother. Tsuneyo is just leagues above everyone but we don't know 'why' yet. There may not be a reason why Tsuneyo may be just that powerful... Soup does soup?...

Regular Moms (B):

Chika: Moving away from tiering into reasoning. Chika leads because she already idolizes her mother, she's been taught so much and exhibits as much in her care for both Chinami and Yumi. (Gary fears her) who knows if it's Nao brainwashing or Chika mother senses on her reaction there... She's caring about so many people already she (would hopefully) not want to be a mother until she was ready many years from now but.. She has the knowledge and exposition, not the means to be a good one.

Ayane: The reverse of Chika. She wants to breed. I personally don't think she would be a good mother off rip because of her money and abandonment issues but I think in a world that Akira actually stayed with Ayane and toned her down she'd be great, but that's also the only reality she'll accept. Her notion of 'i'm going to be a good mother because mine left' is a genuine red flag every day lmao.

Molly: Out of nowhere it might seem but raised by a single father having a child probably forces Molly into a reality she would accept. Understanding the loss of a mother she wouldn't willingly abandon it and her experiences are based on eroge and h games so she'd open herself up to a new world of motherhood and tackle it as it comes...

Osako: Feels more grounded than Wakana in everyday life. They should probably come as a pair but i'm treating this like a solo parent expedition to some extent.

Uta: Has alot of her own conflicts we still don't know but feels very family orientated, child would be very protected?

Moms with help (C):

Rin: Not gonna have a kid in current timeline, if kid happened would have Rika as a resource to care for it. Do not think she could cope on her own and probably couldn't cope with Rika either? She just has a solid support network with her that she could probably evolve as a character if it happened, though disaster would happen fast and first.

Yumi: Disaster timeline, 3 ways this goes with her going to chika/yuki/yakuza and generally everything is bad. She would never let the kid get left on it's own though from her own experiences, but it would likely mean a bad end for chinami/chika

Makoto: COPIUM where Makoto understands that Maki is looking out her the best way she knows how and they reach a compromise that maki tones down on the lewd and makoto tones down on the learning and the child gets to choose for themself...

Sana: Really hard to judge but we can only pray Sara would help.

Karin: Could probably spin shit to be wholesome enough that her parents would help raise and care for any children.

Niki: I don't think she would give up her idol status? But her parents or agents would hide everything they could to prolong her career. Niki herself would probably just say 'fuck it lemme raise my kids lol' She would have enough resources to do so but I think is too reliant on Akira that things would slip buy or she would just buy carers for the kids... it's a real 50/50

Miku: Lacking things is what you want to make up for, she'd be overbearing but genuinely care for any child she had... Depressing af but she has the energy to run it down.

Struggling Mom (D):

Wakana: Bro you can't say you want to die that often. Wakana is not ready or willing to accept children lmao. If she had them though they'd be taught well.

Haruka: MMMM DANGER. I don't really think i can say more here?

Kirin: ENTRAPMENT. Could possibly be a good mom but the reasonings behind it are all fucking awful. She'd also want more attention than her children.

Yuki: Story related. She's getting better but she's got her place down here for reasons. I really hope for a good end here somehow...

Noriko: Too sus. She's grounded af but still willing to give up everything? she's gonna become the most broken puppet and launch other characters forward. She can't handle a child.

Otoha: Will literally just abort the child. Still don't like her and I'm currently biased. Ree. Beach earned you some points but you still suck. I am a good god damn homie and you better fess the fuck up before i get the option to.

Tsubasa: Is probably a good mother but has at this point willingly thrown both her children into a predators dens while offering herself as a substitute for her youngest? Is this a ploy to fuck Akira? is this an entrapment plot? she's fucking scary and while she has some genuine moments with her eldest it's a series of neglectful situations we're exposed to. Nothing she does actually 'feels' motherly and that's probably her biggest draw? .. Amazing character.. Probably bad mother(?)

F:

If you leave any of these characters in a room with a small child they will end up in a box under a tree or worse. Everything is self explanatory. 'But Nao--No. Shut the fuck up. I understand how social services work and to be fair I've suspended disbelief to prevent 95% of this list being on that tier. These are the ones I can't comprehend existing even in that universe yet they somehow do.

Enjoy bad rants and pain.

It's supposed to look like an IPv6 address, which is made up of HexDec.
HexDec is 0-9 and a-f.
There are some rules though.
In an IPv6 address you can omit leading zeros.
You can change 2001:0db8:85a3:08d3:1319:8a2e:0370:7344 into 2001:db8:85a3:8d3:1319:8a2e:370:7344
One time you can omit even a whole 16 bit block ( " :1A0F: " <- i'm a 16 bit block) of zeros, turning them into a "::".
2001:0000:85a3:08d3:1319:8a2e:0370:7344 -> 2001::85a3:08d3:1319:8a2e:0370:7344 or 2001::85a3:8d3:1319:8a2e:370:7344
And then there are subnet masks. (been too long can't remember rn).

The point is: If there is a letter beyond "F" in the riddles IPv6 address then it's not a working/false IPv6 address.
Or if it does not apply to above and beyond rules.

/e
IPv6 is afaik an internationel standard. So no japanese only shenanigans.
The so called ICANN is responsible, at least at the top level, for IP address distribution.

It's supposed to look like an IPv6 address, which is made up of HexDec.
HexDec is 0-9 and a-f.
There are some rules though.
In an IPv6 address you can omit leading zeros.
You can change 2001:0db8:85a3:08d3:1319:8a2e:0370:7344 into 2001:db8:85a3:8d3:1319:8a2e:370:7344
One time you can omit even a whole 16 bit block ( " :1A0F: " <- i'm a 16 bit block) of zeros, turning them into a "::".
2001:0000:85a3:08d3:1319:8a2e:0370:7344 -> 2001::85a3:08d3:1319:8a2e:0370:7344 or 2001::85a3:8d3:1319:8a2e:370:7344
And then there are subnet masks. (been too long can't remember rn).

The point is: If there is a letter beyond "F" in the riddles IPv6 address then it's not a working/false IPv6 address.
Or if it does not apply to above and beyond rules.

/e
IPv6 is afaik an internationel standard. So no japanese only shenanigans.
The so called ICANN is responsible, at least at the top level, for IP address distribution.

posts.content_html_raw:
One Ami-centered event back then that confused me a lot is the No Romeo, or rather how it ended. Now we know better that these two Arakawas can take turn having their minds shut down whenever Sekai was “improperly” brought up. But this event also featured injuries; Sensei (or whoever this narrator is) even joked about Ami bleeding out in bathroom and him keeping her thumb in a jar.
What if by some freak accidents all those were real? That Ami really chopped her thumb off during that short episode? And if true what would it mean?

When explaining how reset works in Prayer Position, Maya claimed that scars, grave injuries, or anything physical are revertible due to the “miraculous” nature of resets; apparently we’ve seen this power at work when Makoto jumped, and when Sensei greeted a mysterious abundance of chickens, hitting his head on the floor and having not a scratch whatsoever.

While it’s unsure if other “hospitalizable” situations: Rin’s deeper cut in Lifejacket, Wakana’s OD, Nodoka’s concussion, and Chinami’s sickness all fall into the same basket, what we've seen so far is not just “everything goes back to normal after a reset”, but “an immediate reverting back to prior states will be enforced if necessary”. We’ve known how this Ctrl Z mechanism did a number on Makoto’s mentality; so what if Ami was the same broken ever since early Ch1 if she recovered her finger as soon as she lost it, and remembered all of that?

This hypothesis is easily overthrown since Ami didn’t look the same amount of broken afterwards, and this state of mind will likely be gone after a reset; thus the whole thing probably was just a minor cut and nothing more, at best a plot attempt to showcase the effect of bringing up Sekai (unless this was a cue to her that you can do whatever she wants without physical consequences; it's hard to tell with Ami). However, how Ami reacted to the cut and the way No Romeo ended was just too eerie to not think about some possibilities.

Click to expand...
That's not 100% correct as far as i've seen.

At first, when the game starts it loads the gui.rpy and or gui.rpyc (<- seems to be intermediate code) among others.
(I'll be assuming that it's only the gui.rpy for simplicity.)
In the gui.rpy is a code block that does roughly the following:
- There is an image file in the game's folders. (*Dorm2Summersomethingsomething*.png, this one is always in the base game.)
- The code opens the file, searches for a specific part in it and loads that data, and this is rather interesting, as a code string.
- That code string is then also excuted.
The new code then:
- Opens specific .png's, like it did with the dormblahblah file, from the care packages.
- This time it's not about code but ID's.
(I don't know how the backend service on Sel's server handles this exactly so lets assume the following:
You buy a care package, it has a special "fresh" .png, in a database on Sel's end that .png get's a unique ID tied to your IP (Hopefully not your IP, because bad), that info/connection get's stored on Sel's end and you get the special .png with an ID, within your **.)
- Code reaches out to Sel's server with the ** ID's.
- If the information stored on Sel's end doesn't match the data the code transmitted -> DRM happens.

So unless you took counter measures like discribed on p1 and have at least one care package installed, the DRM always happens. No special scene or event required.

There's another funny thing about all this.
The reason we got to know about this and spicifically the code behind might be Osako's fault.
Maybe we didn't hear that much of her recently is because she's still in prison for her misbehavior

posts.content_html_raw:
For unknown reason I started to actualy read Yasu's monologues.




So why don't we discuss our unholy trinity once more?

We either still in "Not enough reliable information" phase or there is something interesting here. Trichotomy Callous/Calm/Concerned does not match Everything/Nothing/Rope well, but let Everything/Nothing be on Yasu's perception for now. The point here is that two gods are at war and third is keeping neutralty (common trope, isn't it?)
1) It is interesting because we haven't been given reliable discriminator for who fights for whom yet. Anyway, there is some ideato rely on angels/rabbits color, because why not. With that assumtion, sides of war can be represented by Sekai and Hope.
Yasu god sounds more Sekaish than Hopeish (if we think about them as about different gods, obviously). It also explains rabbits and angels colors mismatch, which is a problem of "default" theory: there is no mismatch, both of them are on "Dark side". I do not like this conclusion, it contradicts the idea that linkage between Hope and Sensei is the reason Yasu calls him her god's favorite.

As an alternative, Sekai can be in opposition to Yasu's god. It does not sounds very natural, but a) we know almost nothing about Sekai's backstory b) from last events, Sekai might be "not callous" more than "Lust Eater".

2) "Default" Unholy Trinity theory seems a bit broken. Especialy in the part when order is important.

We have Callous/Calm/Concerned. We also know it is same trichotomy as "The Lust Eater" / "The Wire God" / "The Dark".
Next, the important part, we assume they are Hope (Nozomu)/Wire god/Pareidolia.

DeSkel mentioned (AFAIR) recently, that "The Dark" does not fit Pareidolia well. The more i think about it, the more I question miself "how do we know that pareidolia is Concerned god"? For all I know, he might be Callous god as well.

Now we also have Everything/Nothing/Rope trichotomy. War between Callous and Calm is strange, and how Callous could be everything? With (1) it sounds more like not understanding what is goind on, than some misinterpritations

Sidenote: If Callous/Calm/Concerned in that order survives, we might suprisingly find that Ami is callous, Maya is calm and Ayane is concerned. It sounds less insane after "Flowerchild"

3) This is not about "default" theories and more about my own thoughts. Initialy i linked existance of Kumon-me to agony of dying god, but now that god is not just dying, but also fights in the war. That not sounds like an agony. If there is a war, it opens some room for Sensei as Faust, who obliged to choose a god to help him win a bet or smth like that. Simple and explains amount of divine interventions in his live

PS by "default" i name theories that I think are common within community. If they aren't, they aren't

PPS Yasu alsmost identified her god with rope in that event. And Sekai with her god. Interesting, isn't it?

Kind of long response revolving around Yasu's 'Frankincense & Myrrh':
Yasu seems to think there's "three great divines":
The black (Everything/light), the white (Nothing/In the dark), and the rope (All that lies between):
Which seems to be Summer/HOPE (Yasu wears black in Summer), Winter/Wire god (Yasu wears white in Winter), and the Rope just seems to be her way of saying reality/perception/the rules, etc:

Yasu, however, doesn't actually seem to know as much as she thinks:
Or at least her god hasn't told her everything. I don't think she's really aware of Pareidolia, or a "third god", so I don't think this "Rope" is related to The Concerned. Yasu's knowledge seems limited to the first 2:
The Rope seems to just be her way of saying "reality itself".

Nao might actually be this "Rope" though, and Sensei could be a thread dangling off of it:
Presumably, like everyone else who sees shit.

Overall, If I had to guess the point of Yasu's rant then: the 2 major gods are fighting over these threads:
And that's why "the rope"/reality is fraying. These threads might be the ones keeping this reality stable, and whoever has more threads, when reality breaks/the rope snaps, will either win the game or everyone loses, and both gods are ignoring the dangers of this:

As for Sekai, I think she's an entirely different beast than these "gods". Whatever is taking her form seems to be "the world itself" that Yasu has brought up in her 'The River Styx' event:
I think Pareidolia has also implied there is a connection between these two (Sekai/The World):
In Yumi's 'Abyss', and the parallels are definitely there:
Overall, when it comes to whatever is taking Sekai's form though, the conclusion seems to be:
And I think it might even be the thing that has been killing and hurting people. From possessing the likes of Kaori and seemingly Yasu, to killing Makoto's father, Todd, and presumably Yumi. If there's anything that we should be wary of, at the moment, it's likely this thing:
I don't think it's really on anyone's side besides it's own.

As for my Pareidolia misinterpretation:
I hadn't realized what actually belonged to Pareidolia. See, it being the third/concerned seems easy enough to put together based off the 'There Is Nothing' Main event, the 'Trinity p3 Non Est Deus' Happy Event and Sana's 'Ad Infinitum':
Since User3/Pareidolia seems to talk the same and has mentioned it was very concerned. There's also how the most recent showing of Pareidolia seemed to have replaced User3 with "pareidolia":
(This also implies the Users/gods can change their names at will, which makes it even harder to trust who is who)

Anyway, what I hadn't realized about Pareidolia was that it's actually the one related to "The Dark" and "Spiders" (I had thought each were a Calm and Callous trait respectively, but I was wrong):
Not to mention, it seems to be the inconsistent god based off the "different parts of other books and pages of all different sizes" part. Also yes, this implies that the "Mistress of the Dark" and the "Queen of Spiders" Kaori has actually been related to Pareidolia this whole time:
She's probably Pareidolia's Yasu or Tsuneyo (Assuming they are the Callous' and Calm's best girls, respectively).

I could probably talk about this shit for days, but to be honest, everything could change with a single update, just by something new being revealed or something old being revealed to be a lie or false truth. Unfortunately, it's been implied that something has been purposely misleading the player/theorists:
And who knows who is lying:
Even this Italic Narrator who seems to actually be The Shapeshifter could be lying.

Yasu's God is HOPE. Therefore, the Summer aspect of an entity I will call refer to as the Trinity. Thus the end of Summer marks the waning of HOPE's power and the rise of Wire's (if things were as usual, Winter got shafted). She then says two seasons were taken.

Why were the seasons taken?


ya "Consumed! By those who wish for a fraction of the omnipotence He possesses! And it is {i}we{/i} who are forced to suffer due to their fruitless pursuit of untapped power!"
ya "The world we love is only the world we {i}hate{/i} as a result of needless tampering with the rules and systems that guide us!"
ya "Picture it! The reds and yellows of the fall! The pinks and blues of springtime! It is as if color itself has been taken from us!"

Consumed by those who wish for a fraction of the omnipotence He possesses? Sounds like Pareidolia literally sucked power from Trinity to grow. As Trinity weakens, Pareidolia and the rest are growing. Keep in mind Yasu used the word "those." Plural. Pareidolia isn't the only one, as itself admits:

"this is actually the most i’ve spoken...probably ever."
"but as the days go by, i become stronger."
"i become capable of more things."
"i’m not the only one growing, though."

Bonus:

"you know, if {i}i{/i} had a season, things like this would never happen."

More Pareidolia-talk:

"good afternoon."
"it has been a long time since i have seen your face. "
"but, unsure of whether or not you can see mine, i am hesitant to say something like “long time, no see.”"
"as you may have noticed, things are beginning to come unraveled. "
"and the reason for this far simpler than you might think."
"the reason is that it is my turn."
"there is sure to be some opposition on both ends of the spectrum, but i once again assure you that i have your best interests at heart."
"i once again assure you that following my lead will guarantee the safety of you and your loved ones."
"but i am aware that those like me are often seen as liars."
"i am aware that we have irrational expectations and demand things of you that are simply not possible."
"but i ask for your trust. and, should that trust be received, what you will gain in exchange for it shall be unrivaled."
"what you will gain in exchange for it is exactly what you have always wanted. so there is no need to refuse at all."
"in me, this new world you have found yourself in will truly be your own — and the illusions of freedom that the others have shown you will evaporate into nothingness."
"it may have seemed in the past that i had abandoned you."
"it may have seemed in the past that the rope was fraying."
"and it may seem, in the present, that this rope is tied around your waist."
"you are being pulled in multiple directions."
"should you do the right thing? or should you do the wrong thing?"
"unaware of what you’re meant to be, you have followed both directions. and, in doing so, you have deviated from the paths you’re meant to follow and created a new you."
"the space between morality and immorality blurs with each thought you think and each person you touch."
"but individuality is a gift. and there is no tangible list you can hold in front of your eyes to figure out if you are good or bad."
"it all comes down to perception."
"you will see what it is you want."
"but if you ask me what i see-"
"i would tell you that i see the future."
"and in that future, you are there."

A couple of points:

"both ends of the spectrum"; refers to Trinity.

Winter got shafted. Pareidolia became strong enough.

Now, reading the text in gold, I felt something relating to what Yasu said, but I'll get there.

Moving on:

ya "One is everything. One is nothing."

with dissolve

The third element is the rope between the two facets of the Trinity, "Pareidolia." Yasu is aware of it.

s "Fine...Go ahead."
ya "Black...White...And all that lies between."

ya "If the rope were to snap, who would be the winner? The one with the largest piece? The one who keeps their feet planted after the tear?"


As the two Aspects of the Trinity maintain a stalemate between them, disregarding a third party, this party consumes them from the inside out. They are dooming themselves in their ignorance.


From Wikipedia:

The word derives from the Greek words pará (παρά, "beside, alongside, instead [of]") and the noun eídōlon (εἴδωλον, "image, form, shape").
The German word Pareidolie was used in articles by Karl Ludwig Kahlbaum—for example in his 1866 paper "Die Sinnesdelierien" ("On Delusion of the Senses"). When Kahlbaum's paper was reviewed the following year (1867) in The Journal of Mental Science, Volume 13, Pareidolie was translated into English as "pareidolia", and noted to be synonymous with the terms "...changing hallucination, partial hallucination, [and] perception of secondary images."

Pareidolia is everything that lies between.

"The rope has a mind of its own! It chooses when it tears and lures those who grip it into believing the outcome is not predetermined!"

This is what I remembered when I read that part in gold in the Pareidolia excerpt. Basically, Yasu is accusing Pareidolia of making false promises and exploiting Sensei. Making Sensei trust it before pulling the rug from under Sensei's feet.

"To preach about the injustices of braided horsehair and carve out a hole in the world so the colors will have a place to return to once the time has come to reclaim them! And that time is approaching!"

To preach about the injustices of the rope... and somehow make the Seasons return to Trinity's control (preferably HOPE's).

The only slight problem I see with this perspective is why Yasu doesn't see the third moon. This could be explained in some ways:

One moon for each entity. So basically HOPE-Wires (Trinity) is the red moon. Pareidolia is either the blue or green moon, and the (another) growing God is the third and last moon (which is the moon that isn't Pareidolia's, therefore either the green of blue moon), which is the God Yasu doesn't know it exists (USER4, the reserved USER).

Therefore Pareidolia was a red herring, a misdirection.

The word derives from the Greek words pará (παρά, "beside, alongside, instead [of]") and the noun eídōlon (εἴδωλον, "image, form, shape").

To preach about the injustices of the rope... and somehow make the Seasons return to Trinity's control (preferably HOPE's).

One moon for each entity. So basically HOPE-Wires (Trinity) is the red moon. "it may have seemed in the past that i had abandoned you."

"and it may seem, in the present, that this rope is tied around your waist."
"you are being pulled in multiple directions."

posts.content_html_raw:
Any skilled swordsman has a massive advantage against an unarmed human.

Tsuneyo, with a (steel) sword, trounces Osako and Ayane (simultaneously). Osako can handily beat an unarmed Ayane-Tsuneyo team. Ayane defeats Tsuneyo unarmed, with some difficulty. Ayane armed with a gun can dominate anyone, supernatural powers excluded (her "gun materialization" skill itself is magical, so... probably other characters have things like that, especially Tsuneyo, who is canonically capable of conversing with birds and is the only daughter of an Eldritch God)

Sensei is similarly capable of conversing with birds. I wonder what's up with that.

All in all, my money is on Tsuneyo if everything's allowed; because I believe her trump card is much stronger than mere gun materialization. Ayane, when limited to unarmed combat, or Osako (if we were to include her). And Tsuneyo again if she's allowed to keep her sword.

posts.content_html_raw:
Here's something people can help me with conjuring up possibilities about the most recent reset.

From the past resets, the situations Sensei was in were more or less depicted as him trying his best to regain consciousness from extremely insane acid dreams. These strange conditions, presented themselves to Sensei and players in the form of puzzles, were likely products of the collapsing existence of Kumon-mi itself.

But this is not what we have during the 5th reset (or least in Untitled). What we see here is Sensei being kidnapped to attend some charade TV program while the world outside is ending. By game design, the ten-questions without a doubt is a reset puzzle. However, by how Sensei finds himself in the situation, it is technically not a reset puzzle. This time the puzzles can't even be summed up to interpretations of breaking oneself out of insanity due to the world ending; the process is hijacked by a certain party (assuming the certain party being team HOPE) that also deliberately sets obstacles under an unknown premise.

It's like if Long Maya didn't kidnap us, then we might actually need to answer some bullshit based on the coffee monologue LOL

We've seen the presence of Gods sprinkled here and there during the previous resets but never this main-focused and forceful. So the question naturally goes to what's their goal this time in particular?

We received our ultimatum at the beginning of the 5th reset regarding our lack of tribute to HOPE. So this may be deemed as some kind of direct intervention/punishment on HOPES's end to have things in its favor again. However, judging from how the whole TV show is structured, it is apparent that Long Maya intends to indefinitely trap Sensei within the time between sleepover to the TV show. Moreover, she might be up for hard resetting Sensei when Himawari bails on factchecking.

wrong answer before reaching checkpoint

wrong answer after reaching checkpoint

when your daughter bails on you (assuming this means a hard reset)

So what is Long Maya trying to achieve here? It is perhaps understandable that she'd consider trapping Sensei indefinitely as a mean to break Sensei into submission, and thus he would walk on the designated path afterwards. So in their scheme is more like the only way out is to yield and submit to HOPE rather than getting all the answers correctly. Because as it turns out, nailing all questions is basically impossible when it comes to Ayane segment.

When Long Maya forces your daughter to shapeshift into Ayane and asks you a question that will break her causality, the message it delivers is that the final segment is purposefully scheduled this way so that at least one of the two followings is ensured: Sensei not surviving this reset or Himawari's existence got got if she actually factchecked her own name, or both.

But if the last question is a hard-scripted fail for Sensei and he is thus doomed for a hard reset regardless, how does this benefit team HOPE and why are we receiving a final warning and a fake deadline at the beginning of Untitled if you don't have a chance to make tribute? Is this just an intimidation tactic? Or is this like HOPE's alternative, to basically get rid off the current iteration that doesn't cooperate anymore? Maybe the assumption of being hard reset is incorrect? Or maybe our understanding to why reset puzzles exist is incorrect?


Some other things not related but still interesting upon revisiting the 5th reset:
- Previously Amiokay is portrayed as some kind of victim to HOPE or to some High Will, but this time I feel like she has succumbed to HOPE and joined its team
- It might just be your daughter doing Tsuneyo's character really well plus some overthinking on my end, but during Tsuneyo's segment it feels like Long Maya is trying to trick her into giving away information regarding Mr. Tojo in the meantime.

and doesn't seem to want him to do more than "dance":
Spoiler
And there was something that seemed to attack the Untitled show after the Shapeshifter left. (This interference may have been what
killed Yumi
)
Of course whether Sensei surviving or not, is a good thing is up for debate. The gods actually seem to want Sensei to succeed though. HOPE itself has helped him to the roof during the first reset:
Spoiler
and The Wire god/User2 helped him during the Second and Third resets, because Sensei seemed to ask it for help back during 'There is Nothing'.
The 4th reset is 'A Life of Prizes' and in that it depends on which god you chose during a survey. Callous, then The Lust Eater helps him get out. Calm, The Wire god does instead. Concerned, then The Dark gives Sensei a way to choose one of the others so that he can get out. It depends on the book you get:
Spoiler
It's however been implied that the main goal of gods is for you to sacrifice others to it:
Spoiler
So, this "Rooftop apocalypse squad" thing might just end up being a future meal. There's also the implication that being defiled is required to make it to the rooftop:
Spoiler
Which could be why Yumi and Tsuneyo didn't make it. So, HOPE wanting Sensei to take something that doesn't belong to him, and well, fuck everything, could be it's way of getting others to the roof for later tributes.
