fdsasdf_p said:
Here's something people can help me with conjuring up possibilities about the most recent reset.

From the past resets, the situations Sensei was in were more or less depicted as him trying his best to regain consciousness from extremely insane acid dreams. These strange conditions, presented themselves to Sensei and players in the form of puzzles, were likely products of the collapsing existence of Kumon-mi itself.

But this is not what we have during the 5th reset (or least in Untitled). What we see here is Sensei being kidnapped to attend some charade TV program while the world outside is ending. By game design, the ten-questions without a doubt is a reset puzzle. However, by how Sensei finds himself in the situation, it is technically not a reset puzzle. This time the puzzles can't even be summed up to interpretations of breaking oneself out of insanity due to the world ending; the process is hijacked by a certain party (assuming the certain party being team HOPE) that also deliberately sets obstacles under an unknown premise.

It's like if Long Maya didn't kidnap us, then we might actually need to answer some bullshit based on the coffee monologue LOL

We've seen the presence of Gods sprinkled here and there during the previous resets but never this main-focused and forceful. So the question naturally goes to what's their goal this time in particular?

We received our ultimatum at the beginning of the 5th reset regarding our lack of tribute to HOPE. So this may be deemed as some kind of direct intervention/punishment on HOPES's end to have things in its favor again. However, judging from how the whole TV show is structured, it is apparent that Long Maya intends to indefinitely trap Sensei within the time between sleepover to the TV show. Moreover, she might be up for hard resetting Sensei when Himawari bails on factchecking.
View attachment 2868093
wrong answer before reaching checkpoint
View attachment 2868094
wrong answer after reaching checkpoint
View attachment 2868095
when your daughter bails on you (assuming this means a hard reset)

So what is Long Maya trying to achieve here? It is perhaps understandable that she'd consider trapping Sensei indefinitely as a mean to break Sensei into submission, and thus he would walk on the designated path afterwards. So in their scheme is more like the only way out is to yield and submit to HOPE rather than getting all the answers correctly. Because as it turns out, nailing all questions is basically impossible when it comes to Ayane segment.

When Long Maya forces your daughter to shapeshift into Ayane and asks you a question that will break her causality, the message it delivers is that the final segment is purposefully scheduled this way so that at least one of the two followings is ensured: Sensei not surviving this reset or Himawari's existence got got if she actually factchecked her own name, or both.

But if the last question is a hard-scripted fail for Sensei and he is thus doomed for a hard reset regardless, how does this benefit team HOPE and why are we receiving a final warning and a fake deadline at the beginning of Untitled if you don't have a chance to make tribute? Is this just an intimidation tactic? Or is this like HOPE's alternative, to basically get rid off the current iteration that doesn't cooperate anymore? Maybe the assumption of being hard reset is incorrect? Or maybe our understanding to why reset puzzles exist is incorrect?


Some other things not related but still interesting upon revisiting the 5th reset:
- Previously Amiokay is portrayed as some kind of victim to HOPE or to some High Will, but this time I feel like she has succumbed to HOPE and joined its team
- It might just be your daughter doing Tsuneyo's character really well plus some overthinking on my end, but during Tsuneyo's segment it feels like Long Maya is trying to trick her into giving away information regarding Mr. Tojo in the meantime.

So, random, but what do you guys think about the girls in the hallways being parallels of eachother?

Maya vs Yumi:

Tsunderes. Both have a specific best friend they center their lives around (Ami vs Chika), apparently break into school when it's dark for reasons (Boxes vs Free Food), have a notable affect on Sensei's mental state, and seem to be estranged from their family. Maya eats more than most, while Yumi seems to eat less than most. Maya seems more manipulative, while Yumi seems more violent. Maya seems to be gifted mentally, while Yumi does not. Maya avoids the Old District while Yumi wanders around it.

Molly vs Otoha:
Rivals in love, who live in their own world that revolves around their interests. Molly cares about others, but feels like an outcast, while Otoha doesn't seem to care about much beyond herself, and feels like she's the only one that's normal. Both seem to see Sensei as an influential figure in their life that they want to imitate to feel better about themselves.

Futaba vs Miku:
Busty vs Washboard... Both try to put others, especially their friends, first, and seem to have insecurities about their bodies. Miku is polyamorous and presumably bi, while Futaba is monoamorous and straight. Miku's parents seem gone, while Futaba's seem fine.

Io vs Touka:
Tomboy who hates socializing, and hates feminine stereotypes. Princess who really wants to socialize, and practices feminine stereotypes. Both seem to prefer a more platonic relationship with Sensei.

Chika vs Rin:
Both are bisexual, but Rin likes girls more than guys, and Chika likes guys more than girls (presumably). Rin skipped ahead, while Chika got held back. More or less opposites in tastes, and when it comes to Sensei. Friend who knows him well vs Girlfriend who doesn't know him well.

Noriko vs Tsuneyo:
Weirdos from the Old District who have a restaurant that's owned by their family, and are protective of those around them. Noriko is experienced when it comes to the world around her, and lives through her emotions, while Tsuneyo is inexperienced when it comes to the world outside of her home, and lives through her rationality. Noriko = Empathy vs Tsuneyo = Sympathy.

Ayane vs Makoto:
Parental issues, but Ayane is missing her mom and has problems with her dad while Makoto misses her dad and has problems with her mom. Makoto's mom was there, while Ayane's mom left her. Both seemed to think they could fuck their issues away. Makoto understood she wasn't enough for Sensei. Ayane thought otherwise.

Kirin vs Yasu:
Both seem to see themselves as servants of lust, except Kirin sees sex as depraved, while Yasu sees sex as sacred. Kirin wants to be noticed and to corrupt others. Yasu wants to be ignored and to save others. Kirin sees Sensei as Horrible like her. Yasu sees Sensei as Worthy unlike her. Kirin's backstory is laughable while Yasu's isn't. Etc. Kirin's the demon on your shoulder while Yasu's the angel. Both want you to fuck others though.

Ami vs Sana:
Tiny girls with daughter like themes, that try to help out a relative who struggles with the loss of someone close to them (Sara vs Sensei). Both lost family, like violence, share the same best friend, and seem to see shit. Sana is more passive and quiet, while Ami is more manic and assertive.

Nodoka vs Uta:
Both seemed to have to become caretakers at an early age, have a specific friend who matters a lot to them, and knows them better than anyone else, and both analyze those around them and write down their thoughts on them. Uta has her Harem ranking, while Nodoka has her notes. Supercomputer vs Dumb Dumb. Uta wants attention, while Nodoka prefers the background. Uta seems more submissive, while Nodoka seems more dominant. Uta wouldn't fuck Sensei behind Io's back. Nodoka would fuck Sensei behind Futaba's back.

Some thoughts on Yasu's Hand of God, or rather some wild guesses on who's speaking through her

It isn't clear to me if Yasu at all acknowledges that her own god can and has spoken through her before. Even if she knows, it still isn't clear if her being confused or uncomfortable afterwards is an indication that she is influenced by something other than her god.
Thus despite the entity referring to Yasu' god as a third person Him, HOPE for now will remain on the table (unless not only one entity spoke through her that night which mega complicated matters)

But what got me into thinking otherwise is the tone and the harsh words of this yelling segment.
"GET REAL, FUCKER" and "Eat shit and die"; though well-deserved, but so blunt, harsh, crude, and...humanly.
Among the candidates of creepy celestial beings, most (if not, all) of them speak in its own metaphorical, divine, and elusive way, yet their goals or means always give me the feeling of "tempting Sensei with some good times" (with the possible exception of Nao maybe). Imagining any of these supernaturals saying something like "GET REAL, FUCKER" somehow feels even more unnatural.

So who with more human origins might speak to Akira this way with zero tinge of love or care in there? Some variants of Maya might be plausible; but with enough biased conjecture on the dynamics of Akira's family of origin, the highest possibility to me belongs to Nozomu Arakawa; the human brother one, not the god one (if such thing is possible). It would be his brother finding his own afterlife in Him, either HOPE of the god with the same name, and finding the chance to yell at his little brother once again like he may or may not had done before in the past.

Without knowing the family dynamics, Akira's parents are also viable options, but that yelling feels more like one-sided fight between brothers instead of bad parenting. Jul 2022 -- Rework released
Aug 2022 -- 1 update, 8 events
Sep 2022 -- 2 updates, 32 events
Oct 2022 -- 2 updates, 27 events
Nov 2022 -- No update
Dec 2022 -- 1 update, 23 events

Jun 2023 -- 1 update, 24 events

Months with 1 update: 15

Months with 35-39 events: 2

Months with 25-29 events: 5

fdsasdf_p said:
Some thoughts on Yasu's Hand of God, or rather some wild guesses on who's speaking through her
View attachment 2875339
It isn't clear to me if Yasu at all acknowledges that her own god can and has spoken through her before. Even if she knows, it still isn't clear if her being confused or uncomfortable afterwards is an indication that she is influenced by something other than her god.
Thus despite the entity referring to Yasu' god as a third person Him, HOPE for now will remain on the table (unless not only one entity spoke through her that night which mega complicated matters)

But what got me into thinking otherwise is the tone and the harsh words of this yelling segment.
"GET REAL, FUCKER" and "Eat shit and die"; though well-deserved, but so blunt, harsh, crude, and...humanly.
Among the candidates of creepy celestial beings, most (if not, all) of them speak in its own metaphorical, divine, and elusive way, yet their goals or means always give me the feeling of "tempting Sensei with some good times" (with the possible exception of Nao maybe). Imagining any of these supernaturals saying something like "GET REAL, FUCKER" somehow feels even more unnatural.

So who with more human origins might speak to Akira this way with zero tinge of love or care in there? Some variants of Maya might be plausible; but with enough biased conjecture on the dynamics of Akira's family of origin, the highest possibility to me belongs to Nozomu Arakawa; the human brother one, not the god one (if such thing is possible). It would be his brother finding his own afterlife in Him, either HOPE of the god with the same name, and finding the chance to yell at his little brother once again like he may or may not had done before in the past.

Without knowing the family dynamics, Akira's parents are also viable options, but that yelling feels more like one-sided fight between brothers instead of bad parenting. This plus the following dialogue would make more sense if it's revolving around the car accident and/or Akira's fucked up relation with Sekai, something Nozomu can be a part of.
View attachment 2875462

As scarily confusing as this event is though, some of Sensei's monologues actually crack me up a bit
View attachment 2875488
View attachment 2875492
In addition to almost uncharacteristically talking down on a girl's boobs, I didn't realize Sensei has what it takes in him to not stick his dick in crazy.
And the idea of Yasu preaching during future H-scenes is just so hilarious (not possessed but actual preaching); her favorite position HAS TO be missionary.
Click to expand...
I'm not entirely sure what's going on with Yasu, but she's actually cussed before:
This:
Might just be a more intense side of Yasu's mentality.
Yasu might even have some split personality stuff going on. For example, this seems to be her "main" identity:
But this version simply seems unaware of the others, like the one that met Sensei in the Hallway, and took him somewhere:
and the one that came afterwards:
Normal Yasu seemed unaware of this whole thing:
And it's not the first time she's been confused by what's going on:
I'm thinking there's currently 3 different Yasu personalities:
The Missionary, The Cultist, and The Follower, with I'm thinking The Follower being the main one.

I also don't think it's something supernatural, technically, possessing her, as when stuff like that happens, the eyes become blank:
Except for Nao who seems to replace their eyes with it's own:

Overall, I'm thinking this new side of Yasu might just be another personality of hers. Possibly brought on by Sekai:
Who seems to share Nodoka's embrace your horribleness mentality:
And Yasu seems susceptible to the influence of outside forces:
Especially from "The World itself":
and World can translate to Sekai. I'm thinking with it's restoration thanks to Sensei, it's influence over Yasu has simply grown, and this more crude Yasu personality is a result.
I could definitely be wrong though, and it might be something entirely different going on.
